epfl-edic-phd-computer-communication-sci.about:
EPFL in Lausanne, one of Europe's top technical universities, runs the EDIC doctoral programme in computer and communication sciences, covering machine learning, systems, security, theory, networking, signal processing and more. Admitted students typically spend the first year rotating between labs before choosing a thesis advisor, and EPFL doctoral students are hired as doctoral assistants with a salary and social benefits.

The next application deadlines are 1 December 2026 and 15 April 2027. Current EDIC students run a volunteer review service for statements of purpose and CVs for applicants who lack mentorship.
highlights: Salaried PhD in Switzerland
Lab rotations in year one
Deadlines 1 Dec 2026 and 15 Apr 2027
epfl-edic-phd-computer-communication-sci.eligibility: Holders of a master's degree (or equivalent) in computer science, communication systems, electrical engineering, mathematics or related fields. Any nationality, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Prepare CV, statement of purpose, transcripts and three references
Apply online to EDIC by 1 December 2026 (or 15 April 2027)
Interview with faculty if shortlisted
epfl-edic-phd-computer-communication-sci.costs: Doctoral assistant salary (Swiss scale) plus social insurance; tuition is minimal.

francis-crick-institute-phd-programme-20.about:
The Francis Crick Institute is Europe's largest biomedical research institute under one roof, a partnership of UCL, Imperial, King's College London, Cancer Research UK, the MRC and Wellcome. Its 2027 PhD programme offers projects across biology, chemistry, physics, computing and medicine; students are registered with a partner university.

Funding covers a £27,715 tax-free stipend per year for four years, tuition fees (including international fees) and research costs. Applications close at 12:00 GMT on 3 November 2026 (references by 10 November); candidates hear by 22 December, final interviews run on 13–15 and 18–19 January 2027 and the programme starts on 27 September 2027.
highlights: £27,715/yr stipend + all fees
International fees covered
Deadline 3 Nov 2026, 12:00 GMT
francis-crick-institute-phd-programme-20.eligibility: Graduates (or final-year students) with a strong degree in a relevant science or medicine. Any nationality, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Choose up to the allowed number of 2027 projects
Submit the online application by 3 Nov 2026 12:00 GMT
Referees submit by 10 Nov 2026
Attend interviews in January 2027 if shortlisted
francis-crick-institute-phd-programme-20.costs: Full funding for 4 years: stipend, fees and research costs.

imprs-evolutionary-biology-plon-phd-2027.about:
The International Max Planck Research School (IMPRS) for Evolutionary Biology is an English-language doctoral programme run by the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Biology and Kiel University. Doctoral researchers work on projects in evolutionary biology, genetics, genomics and theoretical biology (six projects in 2027), with structured training, thesis committees and international peers.

Six doctoral projects are offered for the September 2027 start. You must hold an MSc (or equivalent) by the start date; contacting the principal investigator before applying is encouraged. Shortlisted applicants have online interviews.

Selected candidates receive funding for the PhD (normally an employment contract or Max Planck support contract covering salary and social insurance; no tuition is charged in Germany). The school recruits internationally; the application deadline for the 2027 intake is 10 January 2027, followed by interviews in early 2027.
highlights: Funded PhD contract, no tuition
Topics: evolutionary biology, genetics, genomics and theoretical biology (six projects in 2027)
Deadline: 10 January 2027
imprs-evolutionary-biology-plon-phd-2027.eligibility: Applicants of any nationality (including Georgia and Qatar) with an MSc (or equivalent) by September 2027 in a relevant field and good English.
how_to_apply: Read the open projects and requirements on the school website
Prepare CV, transcripts, motivation letter and referee contacts
Submit the online application by the deadline
Attend online/on-site interviews if shortlisted (early 2027)
imprs-evolutionary-biology-plon-phd-2027.costs: Full funding: salary/stipend for 3–4 years, social insurance; no tuition fees.

max-planck-school-of-photonics-2027.about:
The Max Planck School of Photonics is a joint graduate school of Max Planck institutes, Fraunhofer institutes and leading German universities (coordinated from Jena), covering optics, quantum photonics, lasers and light-matter interaction. Bachelor's graduates apply to the Study Phase (master's followed by PhD) and master's graduates to the Research Phase (PhD). Fellows are funded throughout.

The portal is open until 1 December 2026 for 2027 intakes; you need a bachelor's certificate or preliminary transcript, CV, motivation letter, English proof and two referees (invitations by 1 December, letters by 15 December). Promising candidates take an online test on maths and physics fundamentals and an interview.
highlights: Funded master's + PhD track
Apply with a bachelor's
Deadline 1 December 2026
max-planck-school-of-photonics-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's or master's graduates (or final-year students) in physics, optics, engineering or related fields. Any nationality, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Register on the application portal and choose Study Phase or Research Phase
Upload certificates/transcripts, CV, motivation letter and English proof
Invite two referees by 1 Dec 2026
Take the online test and interview if invited
max-planck-school-of-photonics-2027.costs: Fellowship funding for the master's and PhD phases; no tuition in Germany.

ontario-tech-global-leadership-award-202.about:
Ontario Tech University in Oshawa, east of Toronto, focuses on engineering, computing, health, business and energy. Its Global Leadership Award recognises international applicants studying full-time at a secondary school outside Canada who show strong academic and leadership abilities, and is worth more than CA$120,000 (CA$30,000 a year for four years).

Apply to Ontario Tech (directly or through OUAC; up to three programmes for a CA$100 fee) and submit the Global Leadership Award application by Thursday 11 February 2027.
highlights: More than CA$120,000 over four years
For students at schools outside Canada
Deadline 11 February 2027
ontario-tech-global-leadership-award-202.eligibility: International applicants studying full-time at a secondary school outside Canada with excellent grades and leadership. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to Ontario Tech for fall 2027
Complete the Global Leadership Award application
Submit by 11 February 2027
ontario-tech-global-leadership-award-202.costs: CA$30,000 per year for four years.

oregon-state-international-regional-awar.about:
Oregon State University in Corvallis, through INTO OSU, gives international undergraduates guaranteed Regional Awards based on country of residence, renewable for four years with a 2.0 GPA: $16,000 a year for Europe, Latin America, Indonesia and Singapore (Central Asia $16,000/yr, $48,000 total), $14,000 for India, $12,000 for Vietnam and Africa, $8,000 for Southeast Asia and Hong Kong/Macau, and $2,000 for Taiwan. Students not covered can receive the Provost's Scholarship for Excellence ($6,000/yr, 3.5+ GPA).

Awards are automatic, but students on government or other external sponsorship are not eligible. Values shown are 2025–26 figures and may change; check with INTO OSU for 2027.
highlights: Up to $64,000 guaranteed by region
Automatic, renewable with 2.0 GPA
Provost's Scholarship $6,000/yr for 3.5+ GPA
oregon-state-international-regional-awar.eligibility: Self-funded international undergraduates (first-year, pathway or transfer) at Oregon State. Region determines the amount. Georgia and Qatar citizens may apply (check which region applies).
how_to_apply: Apply to Oregon State through INTO OSU
Award is set automatically by region or GPA
Keep the renewal GPA
oregon-state-international-regional-awar.costs: $2,000–16,000 per year depending on region (2025–26 values).

uottawa-international-english-admission-.about:
The University of Ottawa, Canada's largest bilingual university, offers two scholarships to newly admitted international students in English-taught undergraduate programmes. The International English Admission Scholarship is automatic and unlimited: CA$7,500 per term (up to 12 instalments, CA$60,000 over a four-year degree) for students with an admission average of at least 80% who pay international fees and are not in French immersion. An International English Academic Excellence Scholarship lifts the total to as much as CA$70,000.

Students who choose French-taught programmes can instead receive the Differential Tuition Fee Exemption Scholarship, which reduces fees to the domestic level.
highlights: CA$60,000 automatic for 80%+
Up to CA$70,000 with excellence award
French programmes: pay domestic fees
uottawa-international-english-admission-.eligibility: Newly admitted international fee-paying students in English-taught undergraduate programmes (not French immersion) with 80%+ admission average. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to uOttawa (OUAC 105)
Keep an 80%+ admission average
You are notified of the scholarship at admission
Maintain the renewal conditions each term

western-international-presidents-entranc.about:
Western University in London, Ontario, runs a National Scholarship Program for all-round excellence. International (visa) students are eligible for two parts of it: three International President's Entrance Scholarships of CA$100,000 each (CA$25,000 a year for four years) and the Neen Hodgins President's International Entrance Scholarship (up to CA$100,000) for Arts & Humanities. Interviewed candidates who are not selected still receive a CA$2,000 National Merit Award and keep eligibility for admission scholarships of CA$2,500–8,000.

You need a minimum 90% average, an OUAC application listing Western's main campus, and a nomination from your school (each school may nominate one extra international student). The 2027–28 application opens by mid-November 2026; the 2026 deadline was 14 February.
highlights: CA$100,000 over four years
School nomination required
Application opens mid-Nov 2026; deadline mid-Feb 2027
western-international-presidents-entranc.eligibility: International (visa) students entering Western's main campus in fall 2027 with a 90%+ average and a school nomination. All nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Apply to Western through OUAC (main campus)
Ask your school for a National Scholarship nomination
Complete the online National Scholarship application with your OUAC number (opens mid-Nov 2026)
Submit all documents by the mid-February 2027 deadline
Interview if shortlisted
western-international-presidents-entranc.costs: CA$100,000 (CA$25,000 per year for four years).

aegee-lets-recover-ukraine-eindhoven-202.about:
Organised by AEGEE's Help Ukraine Taskforce and AEGEE-Eindhoven, this one-day thematic event at Eindhoven University of Technology (Blauwe Zaal, 7 December 2026) features Dutch architect Fulco Treffers, co-founder of Ro3kvit, a Kyiv-based urban coalition working on the recovery of Ukrainian cities. The lecture covers the architectural, social and political challenges of reconstruction.

A follow-up discussion with free lunch runs until 15:00, followed by a film screening and a Ukrainian dinner. Up to 30 participants; free of charge, with limited hosting by local members for those travelling.
highlights: Free event with lunch and dinner included
Meet an architect working on Ukraine's reconstruction
Good fit for architecture, urban planning and policy students
aegee-lets-recover-ukraine-eindhoven-202.eligibility: AEGEE members (students and young people, typically 18-35, of any nationality) - you join a local AEGEE antenna first; event language is English.
how_to_apply: Become a member of a local AEGEE antenna (or contact) if you are not one yet
Log in to MyAEGEE and open the event page
Answer the motivation questions and submit the application before the deadline
Confirm your place and pay the fee if accepted
aegee-lets-recover-ukraine-eindhoven-202.costs: Free (fee EUR 0); lunch and an authentic Ukrainian dinner provided; limited hosting by Eindhoven members.

aegee-network-meeting-sarajevo-2026.about:
Network Meetings (NWMs) are AEGEE's regional gatherings organised with the Network Commission. The Sarajevo edition (10-13 December 2026), hosted by the AEGEE Contact in Sarajevo, brings together big and small locals, new contacts and experienced members to exchange best practice in running a student organisation, organising events and engaging members.

With 14 places, a EUR 60 fee including hostel and two meals a day, and a city-centre setting, it is an affordable way to see Sarajevo and build a European network. Applications close 27 November 2026.
highlights: Learn how youth organisations across Europe are run
Explore historic Sarajevo
Affordable: EUR 60 with accommodation and meals
aegee-network-meeting-sarajevo-2026.eligibility: AEGEE members (students and young people, typically 18-35, of any nationality) - you join a local AEGEE antenna first; event language is English.

aegee-network-meeting-sarajevo-2026.costs: Fee EUR 60 covering hostel accommodation and 2 meals a day; travel not covered.

aegee-rtc-krakow-policy-advocacy-2026.about:
This Regional Training Course (RTC), run by AEGEE-Kraków with AEGEE Academy, teaches the key steps of effective advocacy: framing a problem and solution, testing hypotheses through research, writing a policy paper and building a campaign that reaches decision-makers. One trainer is studying public policy and governance; the other works at the Council of Europe.

It takes place 26-29 November 2026 in Kraków for 15 participants, with a European Night, a Polish culture evening with cooking workshop and a games night. Ideal for students interested in NGOs, EU affairs or public policy careers.
highlights: Write a real policy paper and campaign plan
Trainer from the Council of Europe
Small group of 15 participants

aegee-rtc-krakow-policy-advocacy-2026.costs: Fee EUR 70 covering shared rooms (3-4 people) in a conference venue and 2 meals a day; travel not covered.

aegee-safe-person-training-tartu-2026.about:
Organised by AEGEE's Safe Person Committee, Training Committee and AEGEE-Tartu, this training turns participants into 'Safe Persons': trained members who can prevent, detect and react to sexual harassment during AEGEE events and act as multipliers in their local groups. Day one builds knowledge and shares experience; the following days practise concrete skills and response techniques.

It runs 18-23 November 2026 in Tartu, Estonia, for up to 20 participants, with an optional social programme exploring the city. The fee is EUR 40 including hosting and three meals a day. Applications close 1 November 2026.
highlights: Practical safeguarding and anti-harassment skills
Only 20 places, low fee of EUR 40
Become a certified Safe Person for AEGEE events

Confirm your place and pay the fee if accepted
aegee-safe-person-training-tartu-2026.costs: Fee EUR 40 covering accommodation (gym/hosting by local members) and 3 meals a day; travel not covered.

aegee-training-new-trainers-istanbul-202.about:
Training New Trainers (TNT) is AEGEE Academy's flagship course for people who want to become non-formal education trainers. Over a week in Istanbul (29 November - 6 December 2026), 16 participants spend about eight hours a day learning to speak in front of groups, facilitate, design sessions and build a trainer's toolkit, supported by an experienced trainer team.

Graduates join AEGEE's trainer community and can deliver workshops at events across Europe; the skills also transfer to university, NGO and professional settings. Fee EUR 185 with hostel and full board.

Intensive week with experienced head trainer
Join AEGEE's European pool of trainers

aegee-training-new-trainers-istanbul-202.costs: Fee EUR 185 covering hostel accommodation and 3 meals a day; travel not covered.

aegee-winter-madness-novi-sad-2026.about:
Winter Madness is AEGEE-Novi Sad's annual New Year event, now in its ninth edition. For a week (27 December 2026 - 2 January 2027) up to 35 young Europeans explore Serbian and Balkan culture: dance and music, cooking, decorating traditional glasses, humanitarian workshops and discussions that challenge stereotypes, ending with New Year's Eve in Novi Sad.

Accommodation is a central hostel with two meals a day; fee EUR 235. A good intercultural experience for students who want to meet peers from across Europe.
highlights: New Year in Novi Sad with peers from across Europe
Cultural and humanitarian workshops
35 places

aegee-winter-madness-novi-sad-2026.costs: Fee EUR 235 covering hostel accommodation in central Novi Sad, 2 meals a day and programme (incl. New Year); travel not covered.

ala-diploma-programme-2027-entry.about:
African Leadership Academy (ALA) is a two-year residential school near Johannesburg that brings together young people from across Africa and around the world to prepare for university and for leadership on the continent. Students live on campus with peers from many countries and follow a programme built around academic readiness and leadership development.

For the 2027 entry, applicants must be born on or after 1 September 2007; nationality is not a restriction. Applications opened on 15 July 2026; the Early Decision deadline (15 October) has passed, and the Regular Decision deadline is 15 January 2027, with results in April 2027. Selection is holistic (intellectual readiness, courage and perseverance, ownership, interdependence). The all-inclusive cost is USD 30,900 a year, but every admitted student is eligible for need-based aid and 97% receive financial assistance.
highlights: Pan-African boarding school focused on leadership
97% of students receive financial aid
Regular Decision deadline 15 January 2027
ala-diploma-programme-2027-entry.eligibility: Students born on or after 1 September 2007, from any country (Africa and worldwide), finishing secondary school.
how_to_apply: Read ALA's application guide
Complete the online application with essays and school records
Submit by the Regular Decision deadline (15 January 2027)
Complete any further assessment requested and the financial-aid application
Receive results in April 2027
ala-diploma-programme-2027-entry.costs: USD 30,900 per year all-inclusive (tuition, accommodation, meals, uniforms). Need-based financial aid for all admitted students; 97% receive assistance.

auc-arabic-language-intensive-2027.about:
The American University in Cairo (AUC) runs one of the best-known Arabic programmes in the Arab world through its Arabic Language Instruction unit. The Arabic Language Intensive (ALIN) runs during the academic year (with a version for professionals and diplomats, ALID), and the Arabic Intensive Summer Program (ALIS) runs in summer; students are placed by level after a placement test (except complete beginners) and study Arabic intensively, on AUC's New Cairo campus.

Spring 2027 classes run 31 January–27 May (apply by 27 December 2026); summer 2027 classes run 13 June–29 July (apply by 9 May 2027, placement test by 16 May, deposit by 23 May, full payment by 21 June). There is no application fee; applicants submit a recommendation letter and a medical statement, and admission is rolling with limited places.
highlights: Arabic at Egypt's leading English-medium university
Spring semester or summer session options
No application fee; rolling admission
auc-arabic-language-intensive-2027.eligibility: Learners of Arabic (typically university students, graduates and professionals) from any country; placement test required unless a complete beginner.
how_to_apply: Choose spring (ALIN/ALID) or summer (ALIS)
Apply online by the deadline (27 Dec 2026 for spring, 9 May 2027 for summer)
Send a recommendation letter and medical statement
Take the placement test unless a beginner
Pay the deposit and arrange an Egyptian student or entry visa
auc-arabic-language-intensive-2027.costs: Tuition per AUC ALI fee schedule (not listed on the deadlines page); no application fee. Housing and travel extra.

auc-summer-session-visiting-students-202.about:
The American University in Cairo welcomes visiting international students for a semester, a year or the summer. In the summer session (June–July), visiting undergraduates enrol in regular AUC undergraduate courses taught in English and can combine study with life in Cairo. Graduate courses are not offered in summer.

The undergraduate application deadline for the summer session is 1 May; exact 2027 term dates are on AUC's academic calendar. Applicants who want an AUC visiting-student scholarship must apply before the regular deadlines.
highlights: Regular English-taught AUC courses
Combine credit with Arabic and Middle East studies in Cairo
Visiting-student scholarships available
auc-summer-session-visiting-students-202.eligibility: Undergraduate students enrolled at a university outside Egypt (visiting/study-abroad students); see AUC's eligibility page.
how_to_apply: Check the visiting-student eligibility page and summer course list
Apply online by 1 May 2027 (earlier if seeking a scholarship)
Get course approval from your home university
Arrange housing and an Egyptian visa
auc-summer-session-visiting-students-202.costs: AUC visiting-student tuition per credit plus housing; scholarships for visiting students on the AUC Scholarships page.

cern-openlab-summer-student-programme-20.about:
CERN openlab is CERN's public-private partnership for computing research. Each summer its Summer Student Programme brings bachelor's and master's students specialising in computer science and related fields to CERN near Geneva for nine weeks (starting 21 or 28 June 2027). Students work on projects in areas such as AI, quantum computing, data analytics and high-performance computing, each with a dedicated CERN supervisor, attend lectures by CERN experts and partner companies, and finish with a report and a short public presentation.

Participants receive an allowance of 94 CHF per calendar day, a lump-sum travel allowance, CERN health insurance and help finding accommodation. Candidates of all nationalities may apply. Decisions arrive by late March/early April 2027.
highlights: Nine weeks on computing projects at CERN with a dedicated supervisor
94 CHF per day allowance plus travel allowance and health insurance
Open to all nationalities
cern-openlab-summer-student-programme-20.eligibility: Bachelor's or master's students (not PhD) in computer science, mathematics, engineering or physics with a strong computing profile, who will have completed at least 3 years (6 semesters) of full-time university study by summer 2027 and are still enrolled during the summer; good English; no previous CERN summer programme or more than 3 months at CERN.
how_to_apply: Check the openlab page from November 2026 for the 2027 call
Prepare a CV, academic transcript and a motivation statement in English or French (PDF)
Click 'I am interested' on the call page and complete the application on CERN's recruitment system
Arrange reference letters as requested in the call
Replies by late March/early April 2027
cern-openlab-summer-student-programme-20.costs: No fees. 94 CHF per calendar day allowance, lump-sum travel allowance, CERN health insurance; accommodation is paid by the student (CERN helps find it).

euro-space-center-astronaut-camp-english.about:
The Euro Space Center in Transinne, in the Belgian Ardennes, runs residential space camps for young people. The English-language Astronaut Camp lasts six days and five nights: campers train on the multi-axis chair (disorientation training), fly a complete simulated space mission from lift-off and orbit to satellite deployment and landing, and try Moonwalk/Marswalk VR experiences of lunar and Martian gravity, alongside lessons on space science.

The 2027 English sessions are 19–23 July, 2–6 August and 30 August – 3 September. Campers can board (Sunday 5 pm to Friday 4 pm, meals and lodging included) or attend as day students. Booking is by an online pre-reservation that the team then confirms.
highlights: Astronaut training: multi-axis chair, mission simulation, VR moonwalk
Run in English for ages 9–18
Residential option with meals and lodging included
euro-space-center-astronaut-camp-english.eligibility: Young people aged 9 to 18. The camp is taught in English; the booking form accepts participants from any country (check visa needs for Belgium/Schengen).
how_to_apply: Choose a 2027 English session on the Euro Space Center camp page
Select boarding or day camp and submit the online pre-reservation
Wait for the team to confirm and send payment details
Questions: camps@eurospacecenter.be or +32 61 65 01 33 (weekdays 9:00–16:00)
euro-space-center-astronaut-camp-english.costs: Paid camp; the price for boarding or day attendance is shown at booking (boarding includes meals, lodging, T-shirt and astronaut badge). Travel to Belgium not included.

eyp-germany-national-selection-process-2.about:
The National Selection Process of EYP Germany is a three-stage competition that has run since 1990. In the first round, teams of 4-8 young people or individuals aged 15-19 submit a topic outline in English on the 2027 theme (the online generation and digital spaces). A jury of more than 60 people, including Members of the European Parliament, invites the best 22 delegations and 24 individual delegates to Regional Selection Conferences.

The Regional Selection Conferences take place in Munich (10-13 February 2027) and Berlin (21-24 March 2027), each with about 150 young people from all over Europe; the best go on to the National Selection Conference in Leipzig (3-8 June 2027). Winners represent Germany at an EYP International Session. Sessions simulate the European Parliament: teambuilding, committee work on a resolution and a General Assembly debate, plus cultural programme.

The written round is open to young people living in or attending school in Germany. Young people from other countries join these sessions through their own EYP national committee or as volunteer officials (chairs, media, organisers) via the EYP Members Platform.
highlights: Three-stage competition judged by a jury including MEPs
Regional conferences in Munich and Berlin, national final in Leipzig
Winners go to an EYP International Session abroad
eyp-germany-national-selection-process-2.eligibility: Young people aged 15-19 (delegations of 4-8, max one delegation per school, or individuals) who attend school/live in Germany; sessions are in English. International students join via their own EYP national committee.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 guide and selection topic on the EYP Germany page
Write a topic outline in English using the template
Submit it through the online application form by 11 November 2026
If invited, attend a Regional Selection Conference in February or March 2027
eyp-germany-national-selection-process-2.costs: Application is free; participation fees and travel for the conferences are set by EYP Germany (contact mitmachen@eyp.de).

eyp-netherlands-capelle-aan-den-ijssel-r.about:
Capelle aan den IJssel 2027 is one of four Regional Conferences in the 2026-27 season of EYP the Netherlands, held 5-7 February 2027 under the theme "Reimagining Europe Together: Meeting Each Other in the Middle". Friday is the officials' training; Saturday is teambuilding and committee work; Sunday is the General Assembly, where committees debate their resolutions in English following European Parliament procedure.

Delegates are Dutch high-school students (havo/vwo, about 15-18) who sign up as a school delegation or individually; the best delegations are selected for the National Conference in Amsterdam in spring 2027. Officials (chairpersons, editors, journalists, organisers) are EYP alumni from all over Europe who apply through calls on the international EYP Members Platform; the event page has travel information for international participants.

It is a short, low-cost way to practise debating, policy writing and public speaking in English and to meet young Europeans.
highlights: Committee work and a General Assembly modelled on the European Parliament
Path to the National Conference in Amsterdam
International officials welcome via the EYP Members Platform
eyp-netherlands-capelle-aan-den-ijssel-r.eligibility: Delegates: high-school students aged 15-18 in the Netherlands (school delegations or individuals). Officials: EYP alumni of any nationality via the Members Platform.

Register as a school delegation or an individual delegate via the EYP NL Join page
EYP alumni: apply as an official through the call on members.eyp.org
Prepare with the Topic Overviews published before the session
eyp-netherlands-capelle-aan-den-ijssel-r.costs: Participation fee per EYP NL payment procedure; accommodation in the school venue (bring sleeping bag); travel not covered.

Leeuwarden 2027 is one of four Regional Conferences in the 2026-27 season of EYP the Netherlands, held 15-17 January 2027 under the theme "Reimagining Europe Together: Innovation is Key". EYP alumni: apply as an official through the call on members.eyp.org

eyp-netherlands-leeuwarden-regional-conf.costs: Participation fee per EYP NL payment procedure; accommodation in the school venue (bring sleeping bag); travel not covered.

eyp-spain-maritime-international-forum-2.about:
The Maritime International Forum (MIF) is EYP Spain's first event of this scale in five years: a week of committee work, expert input and a General Assembly focused on marine sustainability, Mediterranean protection and the future of Europe's coastlines. It runs 21-28 April 2027 in Castellón and Valencia with about 120 delegates and 50 volunteers from more than 30 countries.

Delegates come through EYP national committees across Europe (including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Ukraine and Türkiye where committees are active), usually after national selection sessions; experienced EYP alumni can apply as chairs, journalists or organisers when calls open on the EYP Members Platform. Ask your national committee early if you want a delegate place.
highlights: Week-long international EYP forum on the Mediterranean and oceans
120 delegates and 50 volunteers from 30+ countries
Partners include institutions and marine experts
eyp-spain-maritime-international-forum-2.eligibility: Delegates: secondary-school students (about 16-19) selected by their EYP national committee. Officials: EYP alumni of any nationality via the Members Platform.
how_to_apply: Contact your EYP national committee and take part in its selection sessions
EYP alumni: watch the Members Platform for officials calls
Follow the MIF 2027 page for programme and academic updates
eyp-spain-maritime-international-forum-2.costs: Participation fee and travel set per national committee; board and lodging during the forum usually provided by organisers.

eyp-spain-university-forum-upf-2026.about:
The University Forum is EYP Spain's first session designed for university-age participants. Over three days at Universitat Pompeu Fabra (13-15 November 2026) participants join a committee built around a real European Parliament portfolio, debate a pressing European or global issue, draft a resolution and defend it in a General Assembly vote.

Day 1 brings an opening ceremony and an expert panel, day 2 committee work and a gala night, day 3 the General Assembly. The only requirement is being 18 or older; no experience with EYP or formal debate is needed, so it is a good first step for international students in Barcelona or anyone who can travel there.
highlights: Hands-on simulation of European Parliament decision-making
Expert panel with institutional guests
Open to any student aged 18+, no experience needed
eyp-spain-university-forum-upf-2026.eligibility: Anyone aged 18 or older; working language English. No nationality restriction stated.
how_to_apply: Open the University Forum page
Fill in the delegate registration form (Google Form)
Wait for confirmation from the organisers (questions: eypupf@eype.es)
eyp-spain-university-forum-upf-2026.costs: Fee (if any) is communicated after registration; travel and accommodation are your own.

eyp-switzerland-rsc-bern-2027.about:
EYP Switzerland's 2027 Regional Cycle has three Regional Selection Conferences: Schaffhausen (5-7 March), Fribourg (20-21 March) and Bern (3-4 April). This record covers the Bern session (3-4 April 2027). Delegates work in committees on current European issues, write a resolution and debate it in a General Assembly, all in English; everyone is welcome regardless of English level.

The sessions are open to young people aged 15-19 in Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The best delegates are invited to the National Selection Conference in St. Moritz (3-7 September 2027), which in turn selects Swiss delegations for EYP International Sessions. The board tries to include as many cantons and schools as possible; selection results arrive by end of January.
highlights: Debate European politics in English with peers from across Switzerland
Path to the National Selection Conference St. Moritz 2027
Teacher guide and delegate guide provided
eyp-switzerland-rsc-bern-2027.eligibility: Young people aged 15-19 living or attending school in Switzerland or Liechtenstein. Officials from other countries apply via the EYP Members Platform.
how_to_apply: Read the Delegate Guide on the EYP Switzerland Participate page
Fill in the delegate application form (rank your preferred RSC)
Submit by 18 January 2027, 23:59 CET
Receive results by the end of January
eyp-switzerland-rsc-bern-2027.costs: Participation fee set by EYP Switzerland; travel within Switzerland at own cost.

fields-undergraduate-summer-research-pro.about:
The Fields Undergraduate Summer Research Program (FUSRP) welcomes carefully selected undergraduates from around the world to the Fields Institute in Toronto for a research experience in the mathematical sciences from 1 June to 31 July 2027. Students work in small teams with a faculty supervisor on a defined project, with orientation, a graduate-school panel, a presentation clinic and final presentations on 30 July. In 2027 some project teams move to Western University in London, Ontario, from 8 June.

The programme is designed to lead to continued research and graduate study, and actively welcomes students from underrepresented groups. The student application form is planned to open on 2 November 2026 on the programme page, where the deadline and funding details will be posted.
highlights: Team research in pure and applied mathematics with a faculty supervisor
Hosted by a leading international mathematics institute
Open to undergraduates from around the world
fields-undergraduate-summer-research-pro.eligibility: Undergraduate students in mathematics or related fields from any country (details and year-of-study requirements in the 2027 application form).
how_to_apply: Check the FUSRP 2027 page from 2 November 2026 for the student application form
Prepare a CV, transcript and statement of research interests
Arrange reference letters as requested
Submit before the deadline posted on the page
fields-undergraduate-summer-research-pro.costs: Check the 2027 call for stipend, travel and residence details (the programme includes residence check-in on 1 June). No application fee mentioned.

heidelberg-laureate-forum-2027.about:
The Heidelberg Laureate Forum (HLF) is an annual networking week in Heidelberg, Germany, where young researchers in mathematics and computer science spend time with laureates of the Abel Prize, ACM A.M. Turing Award, ACM Prize in Computing, Fields Medal, Nevanlinna/IMU Abacus Medal and other top awards. The 14th HLF runs 11–18 September 2027 with lectures, panels, workshops, a poster session and social events.

Undergraduate/pre-master's students, PhD students and postdocs (within five years of the PhD) can apply through a multi-step online application; reviewers are appointed by the award-granting institutions (ACM, the Norwegian Academy and IMU). The foundation books and pays for hotel accommodation and meals for the week; accepted researchers who cannot get travel funding at home can apply for an HLFF travel grant covering travel and visa costs.
highlights: Meet Abel, Turing and Fields laureates in small-group settings
Hotel accommodation and meals covered by the foundation
Travel grants available for those without other funding
heidelberg-laureate-forum-2027.eligibility: Students of mathematics, computer science or closely related fields at undergraduate/pre-master's level (enrolled, not yet holding a master's), PhD students, and postdocs within five years of the PhD (extended one year per child). Open to all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Prepare a CV, motivational statement and transcripts (originals plus English translations)
Ask a professor or supervisor to submit a recommendation letter directly to the application system
Apply at application.heidelberg-laureate-forum.org between 11 November 2026 and 11 February 2027
If accepted (end of April), register and, if needed, apply for a travel grant between 3 May and 23 June 2027
heidelberg-laureate-forum-2027.costs: No fee. Hotel (single room, breakfast) 11–18 September 2027 and meals during the forum covered by HLFF. Travel is self-funded first; HLFF travel grants reimburse travel and visa costs if other funding is unavailable.

hzdr-summer-student-program-2027.about:
Every summer the Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf (HZDR), one of Germany's large national research centres, welcomes international students for eight weeks between July and September to work on a real project in one of its research teams, in areas such as materials research, energy, health (radiation and cancer research) and matter (accelerators, high magnetic fields, lasers). Each student has a supervisor who plans a project; participants also attend selected lectures and lab tours across HZDR and receive feedback at the end.

Students from around the world can apply between 2 November 2026 and 24 January 2027. HZDR pays a salary to cover daily expenses, provides housing in the student guesthouse and gives a travel allowance to Germany depending on place of residence (EU or non-EU).
highlights: Real project in a Helmholtz research team with a personal supervisor
Salary, guesthouse housing and travel allowance
Open to students from around the world
hzdr-summer-student-program-2027.eligibility: Enrolled senior university students of natural sciences, life sciences, medicine, technology or related fields with very good English, who will have completed at least three years of university study by 30 September 2027 and remain enrolled (bachelor's or master's) after summer 2027. PhD students and anyone who has already had an HZDR contract or stipend are not eligible. All nationalities.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online application form between 2 November 2026 and 24 January 2027
Upload transcripts and proof of enrolment (start date and enrolment until at least 30 September 2027) as one PDF
After pressing 'Finish', send the generated link to a professor or senior scientist for the recommendation letter
Notifications are emailed by end of March 2027
hzdr-summer-student-program-2027.costs: No fees. HZDR pays a salary for daily expenses, provides housing in the student guesthouse and a travel allowance (amount depends on EU or non-EU residence). The application form asks you to confirm you cover remaining travel costs.

julich-jsc-guest-student-programme-2027.about:
The Jülich Supercomputing Centre (JSC) at Forschungszentrum Jülich, one of Europe's largest research centres, has run a guest student programme every summer since 2000, supported by CECAM. Participants begin with an introductory course on parallel computing and the Jülich supercomputers, then join a local scientist to work on a current research topic, in fields such as mathematics, physics, chemistry, neuroscience, software tools, visualisation, distributed and quantum computing, and AI.

The programme lasts ten weeks between August and October (2026 edition: 3 August – 9 October) and is held in English. Students receive an expense allowance and must live in Jülich for the whole programme; Forschungszentrum Jülich helps find accommodation, but travel and accommodation are paid by the participant.
highlights: Hands-on research on some of Europe's most powerful supercomputers
Introductory course in parallel computing, then a supervised project
Expense allowance; held in English
julich-jsc-guest-student-programme-2027.eligibility: Students of natural sciences, engineering, computer science or mathematics who have completed their first degree (bachelor's) but not yet finished their master's, with experience in the computer-oriented parts of their subject. A recommendation letter from a university lecturer or professor is required. No nationality restriction is stated.
how_to_apply: Check the JSC 'Apply for the next programme' page from the end of 2026
Prepare a CV, transcripts and a statement of interest in English or German
Ask a lecturer or professor for a recommendation letter
Submit the online application before the deadline (30 April in 2026)
julich-jsc-guest-student-programme-2027.costs: No fees. Participants receive an expense allowance but pay their own travel and accommodation (help finding housing is offered).

mpia-summer-internship-2027.about:
The Max Planck Institute for Astronomy in Heidelberg offers fully funded summer internships in which bachelor's and master's students join a research group and work on a defined project, from exoplanets and star formation to the Milky Way, galaxies and instrumentation. Applicants rank their top five projects from a published list. More than 1,000 applications were received for 2026, so selection is very competitive.

Interns receive a salary of about EUR 1,000 per month net with social benefits, travel costs are supported and the institute helps find accommodation. At least two internships are reserved for candidates from developing countries (per MPIA's attached list). The next call is announced in December 2026 with applications due in January 2027.
highlights: Hands-on research in a leading astronomy institute
About EUR 1,000/month net salary plus travel support
At least two places for students from developing countries
mpia-summer-internship-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students anywhere in the world (not yet holding a master's degree). Bachelor's students must have completed at least four semesters by the start of the internship to qualify for a visa. AI-generated statements are discouraged.
how_to_apply: Watch the MPIA internship page for the call in December 2026
Read the project list and choose your top five projects
Prepare a CV, a one-page research statement, transcripts and the MPIA transcript form
Submit through the online system by the January 2027 deadline (15 January in 2026)
mpia-summer-internship-2027.costs: No fees. Salary of about EUR 1,000 per month net with social benefits; travel costs supported; help finding accommodation (rent paid by the intern).

ms-tcdc-swahili-courses-2027.about:
MS TCDC is a long-established training centre in Arusha, northern Tanzania, known for teaching Swahili (Kiswahili) to volunteers, students, researchers and development workers, alongside courses in leadership and social change. Its Swahili courses combine classroom learning with cultural activities and practice in the community.

The 2027 calendar includes: 2-week Intensive Swahili (Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced; USD 700) starting 18 January, 8 March, 9 August and 11 October; 3-week Swahili Beginner/Intermediate in Arusha (USD 1,050) starting 8 February, 5 April, 6 September, 11 October and 8 November; and 4-week online courses (USD 580) starting 1 February, 5 April, 6 September and 1 November. It is a practical choice before volunteering, research or study in East Africa.
highlights: Many 2027 start dates, on site or online
Learn Swahili in Arusha near Kilimanjaro
Good preparation for volunteering or research in East Africa
ms-tcdc-swahili-courses-2027.eligibility: Anyone wishing to learn Swahili; no nationality restrictions stated. Online courses suit learners anywhere.
how_to_apply: Choose a course level and start date from the MS TCDC calendar
Register with MS TCDC by email or the website
Pay the course fee (and book accommodation at the centre if needed)
Arrange a Tanzanian visa for on-site courses
ms-tcdc-swahili-courses-2027.costs: Intensive 2 weeks USD 700; 3-week course USD 1,050; online 4 weeks USD 580. Accommodation and meals extra.

perimeter-undergraduate-summer-programs-.about:
Perimeter Institute in Waterloo, Canada, the world's largest independent centre for theoretical physics, runs two linked undergraduate programmes. About 30 students attend a two-week Undergraduate Summer School (14–25 June 2027) with courses on modern theoretical physics, research talks and panels. Some are also selected for the PSI Start Research Internship, an in-person paid research placement of 12–15 weeks between 3 May and 13 August 2027 on projects in quantum gravity, quantum information, cosmology, mathematical physics and more.

There are no fees to apply or attend. Summer-school students receive travel support, accommodation and meal credit; interns are paid a research award plus round-trip airfare, housing help and meal credit. Students around the world who meet the criteria may apply; a visitor visa or eTA is normally needed.
highlights: Courses and talks at the world's largest independent theoretical physics centre
No fees; travel, housing and meals supported; interns are paid
Open to students worldwide
perimeter-undergraduate-summer-programs-.eligibility: Undergraduates who plan to apply to a graduate programme in physics starting in 2028 or later and who will have some knowledge of classical and quantum mechanics by June 2027; designed for students in their second-to-last undergraduate year. All nationalities welcome.
how_to_apply: Sign up for an alert on the Perimeter page; the application opens in mid-December 2026
Prepare transcripts, a CV and a statement of interest (up to two pages)
Ask 2–3 referees to submit letters by 30 January 2027
Submit the online application by 17 January 2027 (you can apply to the school, the internship, or both)
perimeter-undergraduate-summer-programs-.costs: No application or programme fees. Summer school: travel support, accommodation and meal credit. Internship: paid research award, round-trip economy airfare, housing at a group rate and meal credit.

segl-johannesburg-semester-2027.about:
The School for Ethics and Global Leadership (SEGL), based in Washington, DC, runs semester-long programmes for highly motivated high-school juniors. Its Johannesburg semester is hosted by African Leadership Academy: SEGL students live and study alongside ALA's two-year Diploma Programme students, take courses in ethics, leadership and international affairs, and keep up honours/AP-level academic work so they return to their home school on track.

The ALA page describes the programme as open to 11th graders from the United States and around the world. Applications (four short writing samples, two teacher recommendations, transcript, a graded History or English paper, parent statement and a faculty interview) and financial-aid requests for Summer 2027, Fall 2027 and Spring 2028 are due 15 February 2027, with decisions on 15 March 2027.
highlights: Live with ALA students from across Africa
Ethics, leadership and global-affairs curriculum
Financial aid available; one deadline for all 2027–28 programmes
segl-johannesburg-semester-2027.eligibility: Students in grade 11 (high-school juniors) from the US and other countries, with strong academic records.
how_to_apply: Read SEGL's Johannesburg programme and tuition pages
Complete the application with four short writing samples
Arrange two core-teacher recommendations, transcript and a graded History/English paper
Submit with any financial-aid request by 15 February 2027
Do the 10–15 minute faculty interview
segl-johannesburg-semester-2027.costs: Semester tuition and need-based financial assistance listed on SEGL's Tuition and Financial Assistance page.

stony-brook-garcia-summer-research-2027.about:
The Garcia Research Scholars Program at Stony Brook University (New York) is an interdisciplinary summer research programme that pairs high-school students with faculty, graduate students and undergraduates on projects in materials science, polymers, medicine, energy and computation. A goal of the summer is to take projects far enough for students to submit abstracts to the Materials Research Society (MRS) Fall Meeting, where accepted work is presented.

The 2026 programme ran 24 June – 7 August. International students are welcome, but the Garcia programme cannot sponsor visas: applicants must already have documents allowing them to be legally present in the US for the programme period. The programme also accepts undergraduates and teachers.
highlights: Real lab research with possible presentation at the MRS Fall Meeting
Interdisciplinary materials, polymer and nanotech projects
International students accepted if they can be legally present in the US
stony-brook-garcia-summer-research-2027.eligibility: High-school students at least 16 years old by early July of the programme year, with an unweighted GPA of about 95/100 (3.8/4.0) and strong science/maths coursework. International students may apply but the programme cannot support visa applications.
how_to_apply: Check the Garcia Apply page in winter 2026/27 for the 2027 application
Complete Part 1 and Part 2 of the online application
Have your school send transcripts and three recommendation letters (one from a science teacher) directly
Pay the non-refundable USD 50 registration fee
Decisions are usually released in early April
stony-brook-garcia-summer-research-2027.costs: 2026: laboratory usage fee USD 4,000 (not including room or board); optional campus room about USD 2,599 for the programme; mandatory health services fee USD 66; optional meal plan. No financial aid or scholarships offered.

uchicago-pre-college-research-practicum-.about:
The University of Chicago's Pre-College 'Practicum' track offers intensive, hands-on research courses. In Research in the Biological Sciences (RIBS), students learn advanced laboratory techniques used in molecular and cell biology and carry out experiments in UChicago lab facilities. In Stones and Bones, students spend four weeks with Field Museum palaeontologists in Chicago and on fieldwork in Wyoming, learning how fossils are collected, analysed and conserved.

Practicum courses are fully residential on the UChicago campus (no remote option) and are for current 10th and 11th graders aged at least 15. Practicum applicants must apply by the priority deadline (13 January 2027). International students are welcome but must check UChicago's visa requirements for their programme type.
highlights: Real lab techniques in a top research university (RIBS)
Palaeontology fieldwork in Wyoming with the Field Museum (Stones and Bones)
Need-based partial aid available, including for international families
uchicago-pre-college-research-practicum-.eligibility: High-school students currently in 10th or 11th grade (or equivalent), at least 15 years old. International students may apply (visa requirements apply).
how_to_apply: Use the Course Finder to choose RIBS or Stones and Bones
Complete the online application by 13 January 2027 (priority deadline required for Practicum)
Upload transcripts for grades 9–11 and a current grade report, and request a teacher/counsellor recommendation
Pay the USD 75 application fee (waived if you apply for financial aid)
Decisions are released in mid-March 2027
uchicago-pre-college-research-practicum-.costs: Practicum programme fee USD 15,200 (2026 figure) including residence. Need-based partial aid (for household income ≤ USD 125,000 the 4-week practicum cost was USD 7,600; ≤ USD 80,000 USD 3,800). USD 75 application fee. Travel and visa costs extra.

uchicago-summer-session-pre-college-2027.about:
University of Chicago Summer Session offers high-school students several pre-college formats: residential Enrichment (short academic experiences), Career Insight (faculty- and industry-led courses), Immersion (undergraduate-level courses taught by UChicago faculty with projects and field trips), the research Practicum, and remote options such as 3–5-week Summer Online courses taken alongside UChicago undergraduates.

Applications for summer 2027 have two deadlines: priority on 13 January 2027 and regular on 3 March 2027. The application asks for transcripts, a recommendation and short responses; some STEM courses ask for test scores. International students may apply and should check UChicago's visa guidance for residential programmes.
highlights: Wide choice of residential and online courses, including STEM and economics
Immersion courses are taught at undergraduate level by UChicago faculty
Need-based partial aid for domestic and international families
uchicago-summer-session-pre-college-2027.eligibility: High-school students (typically grades 9–11 depending on programme; Practicum is 10th–11th grade). International students welcome, subject to visa requirements.
how_to_apply: Use the Course Finder to choose a programme and course
Apply online by 13 January 2027 (priority) or 3 March 2027 (regular)
Upload transcripts and a 2026–27 grade report; request a recommendation
Pay the USD 75 application fee (waived if applying for aid)
Apply for aid by the priority deadline; awards are limited
uchicago-summer-session-pre-college-2027.costs: 2026 fees: Enrichment USD 3,000; Career Insight USD 5,890; Immersion USD 9,300; Practicum USD 15,200; Summer Online USD 4,980. Need-based partial aid available. USD 75 application fee. Travel and visa costs extra.

weizmann-kupcinet-getz-summer-program-20.about:
The Kupcinet-Getz International Summer Program brings outstanding science students from around the world to the Weizmann Institute of Science in Rehovot, Israel, to work for eight weeks (16 June – 12 August 2027) as members of a research group. Each student is matched with a host lab in the faculties of Chemistry, Life Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science, or Physics, based on up to five research topics chosen in the application. Weekends include organised trips around Israel.

There are no application, registration or tuition fees. Participants receive a USD 1,100 stipend, up to USD 400 towards flights, free accommodation for international students in dormitories near the campus, medical insurance and partial meal subsidies. Selection is by the Weizmann School of Science based on CV, transcript, motivation letter and recommendation letters.
highlights: Real lab research at one of the world's leading research institutes
No fees; USD 1,100 stipend, free housing and up to USD 400 flight subsidy
Matched to a host lab by your chosen research topics
weizmann-kupcinet-getz-summer-program-20.eligibility: Bachelor's or master's students (not PhD) who have completed at least the first year of study, or recent bachelor's graduates planning further study, in physical sciences, chemistry, life sciences, mathematics or computer science. GPA of about 3.6/4.0 or equivalent and fluent English required. Open to students of all nationalities.
how_to_apply: Prepare a CV with a passport-size photo, official transcript (with English translation if needed), passport title page and a one-page motivation letter
Apply online between 20 December 2026 and 20 January 2027 and choose up to five research topics
List at least one academic referee; they upload the letter through the link the system emails them
Results are announced in March 2027
weizmann-kupcinet-getz-summer-program-20.costs: No application or tuition fees. Stipend USD 1,100 (two instalments), flight subsidy up to USD 400, free accommodation for international students, medical insurance and partial meal subsidies.

wharton-essentials-of-entrepreneurship-2.about:
Essentials of Entrepreneurship is a selective two-week residential programme on the Wharton campus in Philadelphia. Students learn the basics of starting a venture (innovation, customer discovery, prototyping and pitching) through classes with Wharton instructors and team work, and finish with a pitch competition; completers receive a Wharton Global Youth Certificate of Completion. No business background is required.

2027 sessions: 6–19 June, 20 June–3 July, 11–24 July and 25 July–7 August. It is for students currently in grades 9–11 and international applicants are welcome. Priority deadline 27 January 2027, final deadline 19 March 2027. The 2027 fee is USD 8,599 plus a USD 100 application fee.
highlights: Four session dates across the summer
Team startup pitch competition
International applicants welcome
wharton-essentials-of-entrepreneurship-2.eligibility: Students currently in grades 9–11 from any country; no business background needed; good English required.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and pick a session
Submit the Wharton Global Youth application from November 2026 (USD 100 fee)
Apply by the 27 January 2027 priority deadline
Arrange a US visa once admitted
wharton-essentials-of-entrepreneurship-2.costs: 2027 fee USD 8,599 plus USD 100 application fee; travel and visa extra. Scholarships limited to specific groups; fee waivers not available to international applicants.

wharton-innovation-and-startup-culture-2.about:
Innovation and Startup Culture is a two-week residential programme from Wharton Global Youth that provides a whirlwind introduction to new-venture creation. Students learn how entrepreneurs generate ideas and turn them into high-growth ventures, then develop and pitch their own startup concepts; no formal business background is needed.

2027 sessions run 20 June–3 July and 11–24 July. It is for students currently in grades 9–11 and international applicants are welcome. Priority deadline 27 January 2027, final deadline 17 March 2027. The 2027 fee is USD 8,599 plus a USD 100 application fee. (The programme page lists Philadelphia but also mentions Wharton's San Francisco campus in its schedule, so confirm the location.)
highlights: Startup ideation and pitching at Wharton
Two session dates
International applicants welcome
wharton-innovation-and-startup-culture-2.eligibility: Students currently in grades 9–11 from any country; no business background needed; good English required.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and pick a session
Submit the Wharton Global Youth application from November 2026 (USD 100 fee)
Apply by the 27 January 2027 priority deadline
Arrange a US visa once admitted
wharton-innovation-and-startup-culture-2.costs: 2027 fee USD 8,599 plus USD 100 application fee; travel and visa extra. Scholarships limited to specific groups; fee waivers not available to international applicants.

whoi-summer-student-fellowship-2027.about:
The Summer Student Fellowship (SSF) at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution, on Cape Cod in Massachusetts, gives undergraduates a full summer of independent research in ocean science and engineering. Each fellow works on a project with a WHOI scientist or engineer, attends a lecture series introducing the many sides of marine science, and presents results at the end. Projects span biology, chemistry, geology, geophysics, physical oceanography, engineering, mathematics, meteorology and more.

The programme lasts 10–12 weeks. In 2026 the stipend was USD 721 per week plus a travel allowance of up to USD 720, and housing is arranged by WHOI. International students may apply: WHOI's foreign national adviser helps with the J-1 visa (proof of English proficiency required), and a 14% US federal tax is deducted from international fellows' stipends.
highlights: Independent research project with a WHOI scientist or engineer
Weekly stipend (USD 721/week in 2026) plus travel allowance
International students eligible; J-1 visa support
whoi-summer-student-fellowship-2027.eligibility: Undergraduates who will have completed their junior (third) year by the start of the fellowship; students graduating before the fellowship starts are not eligible. Any science or engineering field. International students may apply (English proficiency proof needed for the visa).
how_to_apply: Browse the potential projects list and identify possible advisers
Apply online between early December 2026 and 1 February 2027 (11:59 pm EST)
Submit short essays on research interests, a CV and unofficial transcripts
Arrange two references through the WHOI references system
Decisions are sent in mid-March
whoi-summer-student-fellowship-2027.costs: No fees. Stipend of USD 721 per week (2026 rate) for 10–12 weeks, travel allowance up to USD 720, housing arranged. International fellows have 14% US federal tax deducted.
